item.text: The sources support the main lifecycle. I’ll distinguish the workflow’s full hunk-coverage check from the general ready gate, and qualify the seed’s claims about pinned source reads and atomic publication where their implementations aren’t supplied.

The central tree is now 37% shorter by line count and 39% shorter by character count. Six peripheral trees add detail from the sources. I’m checking the line anchors and spacing before returning the JSON.

Six peripheral trees expand workflow access and lifetime, push intake, evidence identities, concurrency and recovery, persistence, and review. The trees mix modular boundaries, calls, ownership and concrete data requirements; indentation groups concepts, while edges connect central concepts to their details. New source-grounded details include interrupted-run reporting (diffSessionWorkflowService.ts), the oversized default DiffTree fallback and mapping-only updates (diffTree.ts), manifest-token ownership and 16-entry caches (diagramChangeSessionStore.ts and changeSessionRecords.ts), and preview worker cleanup and acceptance retry IDs (ChangeSessionPreview.tsx). Corrections: edits do not invariably leave a session in draft; ChangeSessionService.update can edit, set draft, then validate and set ready in the same call. Acceptance checks session version and live document content/name, not capturedVersion; it passes savedRevisionId to the catalog. Full hunk coverage belongs to complete_diff_session, not the general validateReady gate. Default commit grouping has a single-node fallback when ASCII exceeds 20000 characters. Uncertainty: only the supplied snapshot was used. The point describes atomic catalog publication, but the catalog implementation is absent; the diagram marks that boundary without asserting a verified transaction.
